faq.question: How do I use this scientific calculator?
faq.answer: Tap the keys or type on your keyboard to build your sum, then press = or Enter. The top line shows what you typed and the large line shows a live answer as you go. Press ⌫ to remove the last entry and AC to start again.

faq.question: How do I switch between degrees and radians?
faq.answer: Choose Deg or Rad above the keys before you use sin, cos, tan, or their inverses. Deg suits school geometry and everyday angles. Rad is the standard for calculus and physics.

faq.question: How do I work out powers and roots?
faq.answer: Use the xʸ key for any power, so 2 xʸ 10 gives 1024. The √x and ∛x keys work on the number you type next. For any other root, type the degree first, press ʸ√x, then type the number: 4 ʸ√x 81 gives 3.

faq.question: What does the Ans key do?
faq.answer: Ans holds your last answer. After you press =, pressing an operator such as + or × carries on from that answer automatically, and your last eight answers stay in the history list below the keys.
